skill.name: verification-before-completion
skill.description: Requires evidence from builds, tests, execution, or cited sources before an assistant claims work is complete.
skill.summary: Adds a final verification checklist before completion claims.
skill.author: ANcpLua

content.value_statement: AI assistants can report work as complete before evidence is available. This skill requires build, test, source, and output checks before any completion claim.
actual_capabilities: Triggers before common completion phrases such as done, fixed, and works.
Provides checklists for code changes, factual claims, bug fixes, and works claims.
Requires build and test results or an explicit reason when tests are skipped.
Prompts source citation or web verification for date, version, and status claims.
Defines a completion report format with status, performed steps, and confidence.
limitations: It does not execute tools by itself.
The command examples focus on .NET and npm workflows.
It cannot prove behavior that was not tested.
It can add process overhead for small tasks.

use_cases.title: Verify Code Fixes
use_cases.description: Require build, test, and reproduction evidence before reporting a bug fix as complete.

use_cases.title: Review Assistant Claims
use_cases.description: Add a final evidence check before accepting an assistant response in a code review workflow.

use_cases.title: Validate Technical Answers
use_cases.description: Require source checks for claims about versions, dates, support status, or platform behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Small Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Before you say this fix is complete, use the verification-before-completion skill. Show what you ran, what passed, and what remains unverified.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the verification-before-completion skill for this feature. Include build status, test status, one edge case, and a clear confidence statement.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Completion Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Review your previous answer with the verification-before-completion skill. Identify any unsupported completion claims and replace them with verified evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Release Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the verification-before-completion skill as a release gate. Define required checks, acceptable skipped-test reasons, and the final completion wording.

output_examples.input: The assistant says a null reference bug is fixed.
output_examples.output: The response includes the reproduced issue, build result, targeted test result, and a confidence note before saying the bug is fixed.

output_examples.input: The assistant says a React component works after a change.
output_examples.output: The response shows a run result, visible render evidence, empty state coverage, error state coverage, and any remaining risk.

output_examples.input: The assistant claims a framework version supports a feature.
output_examples.output: The response cites a current source, states the verified version, and avoids a completion claim if evidence is missing.

best_practices: Run the smallest meaningful verification command before claiming success.
State skipped checks with a clear reason and remaining risk.
Separate verified facts from assumptions in the final response.
anti_patterns: Do not say a fix works without running a relevant check.
Do not hide failed or skipped tests behind a completion claim.
Do not use stale memory for version or status claims.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It tells the assistant to run appropriate checks before making a completion claim.

faq.question: Is this skill only for .NET projects?
faq.answer: No. The examples include .NET, but the verification pattern applies to any stack.

faq.question: Can tests be skipped?
faq.answer: Yes, but the assistant must explain why and state the remaining risk.

faq.question: Does it help with non-code claims?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires sources or current lookup for claims involving dates, versions, and support status.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when assistant accuracy, evidence, and clear completion status matter.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect a short verification checklist with build status, test status, performed steps, confidence, and remaining gaps.
